text.p: - Slovenia's Constitutional Court on Wednesday dismissed a request by Shell Slovenia to lift restrictions on the ownership of motorway petrol stations.
- Slovenia's Smelt Olimpija lost the sixth round basketball EuroLeague match against Greek Panathinaikos 76-74 on Wednesday.
- Slovenian Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun on Wednesday welcomed the outcome of the U.S. elections, stressing good relations between the two countries during the previous Bill Clinton presidency.
- About 70 foreign and more than 100 domestic journalists will cover Sunday's general election in Slovenia, the government's information office said.
- The government will discuss the increase of electricity prices next week. The price would be lifted in two phases, each time by 10 percent, state secretary of trade said on Wednesday.
- More than 48,000 new students entered Slovenia's universities this year -- 2,000 more than in 1995.
- Doctor's Association of Slovenia said 257 doctors applied to set up private practices this year.
- 770 companies have already completed privatisation, while another 1,307 companies are still in the process, state secretary in charge of privatisation Edo Pirkmajer said.
